newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt traders position for jobs data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt traders position for jobs data.

text.p: Traders in U.S. debt options Tuesday were staking out positions with an eye toward Friday's U.S. employment report, floor brokers said.
In options on U.S. Treasury bond futures, those doing the positioning were mainly trading houses, but a few institutional firms also conducted transactions of notable size, the floor traders said.

Among the larger deals was a purchase of 3,000 July 108-00 puts in a spread against the 110-00 puts that was assembled over several hours, traders said. Another house sold 3,000 September 104-00 puts.
On the institutional side, a European banking firm sold 2,000 September 106-00 puts, and a New York dealer bought 1,000 July 111-00 calls and 1,000 August 111-00 flexible calls.

Implied volatilities for bond options softened slightly as the underlying futures languished in a narrow range before the important Friday report. September bond futures settled 11/32 higher at 110-03.
July options volatility was pegged at 8.75 percent and September at around 8.50 percent, still above recent ranges.

Until this week, July had been hovering in a tight range of 8.2 percent to 8.5 percent, but was now drawing support from the uncertainty traditionally associated with the payroll data, said a floor trader at a U.S. brokerage firm.

"It will either remain where it is until the end of the week or go higher," the trader said. He predicted futures would continue to move erratically, with direction in limbo before Friday's big event.
"Tomorrow we're going to have to thrash it out some more," he said.
May nonfarm payroll growth was forecast at 219,000, and the unemployment rate was expected to rise 0.1 point to 5.0 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

Eurodollars options trading was a mixture of put and call buying, reflecting the split in market opinion over the Federal Reserve's next likely course of action on short-term interest rates, a floor broker said.
Low volatility levels overall show the market believes the Fed is not in a sustained tightening mode regardless of what it decides to do at its July 1-2 policy meeting, the broker said.
September Eurodollar volatility was roughly steady at 8.9 percent, with December holding in at 10.7 percent.
A U.S. house bought 5,000 September 94.00 straddles in what was thought to be covering of a short volatility position.
